chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said:

I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام saying: “If a man were brought to me who had accused a Muslim slave of zinā, and we knew nothing of him except goodness, I would administer to him the hadd, the hadd of a free person, except for one lash.”

key_terms.خَيْرًا: goodness; upright conduct known of the person
key_terms.قَذَفَ: to accuse someone of illicit sexual intercourse falsely or slanderously

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for falsely accusing a Muslim slave of zinā in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning slanderous accusation of zinā against a Muslim slave of known good standing. It indicates that such an accusation incurs a hadd punishment nearly equal to that for accusing a free person, showing the seriousness of violating a Muslim’s honor and reputation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5080 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abd Al-Rahman from Ubayd ibn Zurarah who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (as) say, "If a man were brought to me who had accused a Muslim slave of adultery, and we knew nothing about the slave except goodness, I would administer the legal punishment upon him - the same punishment as for a free person, except one lash less."
